question.problem: Which value of $m$ satisfies the equation $\frac{4m+1}{3m}-\frac{m-1}{6m}=\frac{1}{9m}?$
question.worked_solution:
We note that $m=0$ cannot be a solution since division by $0$ is undefined. 

The equation has the denominators $3m,6m,$ and $9m.$ So first, we find the least common multiple (or $\text{LCM}$) of the denominators. We find that

$$
\text{LCM}(3m,6m,9m)=18m.
$$

So, we multiply both sides of the equation by $18m,$ and simplify: 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4m+1}{3m}-\frac{m-1}{6m} & =\frac{1}{9m} \\ 18m\cdot (\frac{4m+1}{3m}-\frac{m-1}{6m}) & =18m\cdot (\frac{1}{9m}) \\ 18m\cdot (\frac{4m+1}{3m})-18m\cdot (\frac{m-1}{6m}) & =18m\cdot (\frac{1}{9m}) \\ 6\cdot 3m\cdot (\frac{4m+1}{3m})-3\cdot 6m\cdot (\frac{m-1}{6m}) & =2\cdot 9m\cdot (\frac{1}{9m}) \\ 6\cdot \cancel{3m}\cdot (\frac{4m+1}{\cancel{3m}})-3\cdot \cancel{6m}\cdot (\frac{m-1}{\cancel{6m}}) & =2\cdot \cancel{9m}\cdot (\frac{1}{\cancel{9m}}) \\ 6(4m+1)-3(m-1) & =2\end{aligned}
$$

We now have a linear equation in $m,$ and we can solve this using the addition and multiplication principles:

$$
\begin{aligned}6(4m+1)-3(m-1) & =2 \\ 24m+6-3m+3 & =2 \\ 21m+9 & =2 \\ 21m & =-7 \\ m & =-\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we recall that we cannot allow $m=0$ as a solution. But since $m=-\frac{1}{3}\ne 0,$ we conclude that the solution is $m=-\frac{1}{3}.$
